description: Some monsters are healed by the element they are aligned with rather than damaged by it, such as lava strykewyrms under fire spells and the Falador elemental wizards under their own element. The engine has no way to express negative damage, so it models the case as immunity. The trap is that the healing element is often the one that otherwise looks strongest; the spell picker never offers it, and this rule is what catches the powered staves that go around the picker. Which element heals which monster lives in the healing element group of the monster families table.

quotes: Fire spells will heal them equal to the amount hit.
The elemental wizards south of Falador are now healed by their own element and damaged by all others.

description: Leafy monsters such as Turoth and Kurask can only be damaged by leaf-bladed weapons, broad ammunition, or the Magic Dart spell, one way through per combat style. The immunity is keyed off the leafy attribute; broad ammunition must actually be fired by the equipped weapon, which is the ordinary ammo-compatibility rule, and Magic Dart is why the slayer staff family exists.

quotes: they can only be damaged with leaf-bladed weapons, broad ammunition, or the Magic Dart spell

description: Flying monsters take no melee damage except from polearms, so the immunity is keyed off the flying attribute, which catches the ones a name list would miss such as Vespula and reanimated aviansies; Zulrah sits in a separate halberd-reach family, needing the same reach for a different reason. The salamander escape is narrowed to the family of targets whose own articles still name salamanders, since the Grotesque Guardians article and Vespula's 6 August 2025 change both allow halberds alone. Not modelled: splash damage from scythes or bulwarks onto airborne targets, and weapon reach in tiles.

quotes: immune to melee damage except for polearms
It cannot be reached with melee (with the exception of halberds).
Dawn is flying and cannot be targeted by non-halberd melee weapons
Halberds can now do damage to Vespula when flying.

description: Vampyres are split across three caste attributes so that a tier-1 quest boss like Count Draynor is told apart from the higher ones: tier 1 takes full damage from any weapon, tier 2 takes nothing from regular weapons unless Efaritay's aid is worn, and tier 3 only from specific silver weapons. The rod of ivandis reaches tier 2 only, so it is excluded from the general melee vampyrebane escape; the blisterwood stake is the Ranged way through and is checked first, since a thrown stake is not a melee vampyrebane. Silver bolts are an ammo-slot item fired from iron crossbows or better, so the tier-2 Ranged escape reads the ammo slot. Efaritay's aid unlocks weaponry rather than casting, so its escape excludes Magic; the blisterwood flail article states flatly that no spell damages a vampyre of any tier.

quotes: All weapons deal full damage
Regular weapons deal no damage unless using an Efaritay's aid
Only specific silver weapons deal full damage
one of the few ammo types able to be used to effectively kill Vampyre Juvinates
from iron crossbows or better
It is also one of the weapons that is capable of killing tier 2 vampyres.
it allows non-silver weaponry to be used against Tier 2 vampyres, albeit dealing half their usual damage
no spells are capable of dealing damage to vampyres

description: The Kraken cannot be reached by melee weapons and is entirely immune to melee attacks, so every melee loadout scores zero against it. Its Ranged reduction to a seventh is the separate KrakenRangedResistance row.

quotes: The Kraken cannot be reached with Melee weapons, and is additionally entirely immune to melee attacks
Magic is the only reliable way of damaging it, as Ranged deals 1/7th of its normal damage.

description: Each Theatre of Blood nylocas takes damage only from the one combat style its carapace colour names, blue for magic, green for ranged and white for melee, and the wrong style is reflected back at the player. The three Nylocas Prinkipas forms carry the same rule and are keyed by monster id because they share a single name. Not modelled: Nylocas Vasilias itself, whose four form ids are shipped as one row, so no form can be told from another.

quotes: Each spider is immune to damage outside of their combat style - ranged must be used against the Toxobolos, magic against the Hagios, and melee against the Ischyros.

with their active combat style and weakness changing according to the colour of their carapace: blue for magic, green for ranged and white for melee. Attacking them with the wrong combat style will cause them to reflect the hit back towards the player as well as healing from the hit.
Vasilias changes its combat style throughout the fight by changing its carapace, which also indicates its weakness: blue for magic, green for ranged and white for melee.

description: Dusk is immune to everything but melee, so no Ranged or Magic loadout scores against it. The immunity takes precedence over the earth-spell elemental weakness its stat block lists.

quotes: Dawn is flying and cannot be targeted by non-halberd melee weapons, while Dusk is completely immune to magic and ranged damage.
Dusk now has a 40% elemental weakness to earth spells (despite being immune to Magic) and -1 flat armour.

description: Salarin the Twisted can be damaged only by Strike spells; melee, Ranged and every other spell do nothing to him. Not modelled: the ring of recoil and dynamite damage that also hurt him.

quotes: Salarin can only be damaged by Strike spells, ring of recoil damage, and dynamite(p).
Salarin must be killed with Strike spells; melee and ranged cannot harm him, nor can any other magic attacks.

description: Surok Magis has Protect from Melee and Protect from Missiles up together and is immune to powered staves, so only a cast spell damages him. Not modelled: his immunity to the sapping effects of blood spells, which the steady-state model has no notion of.

quotes: Surok has 450 hitpoints, attacks with Fire Surge, and has both Protect from Melee and Protect from Missiles simultaneously active. It is therefore necessary to attack with magic.
Surok is notably immune to damage from powered staves, thus the player must use combat spells in order to damage him.
He is also immune to the sapping effects caused by blood spells.

description: Kamil takes magic damage only from fire spells and Fareed only from water spells; every other spell is stopped outright. Fareed also disarms anyone who attacks him in melee range without ice gloves, which a steady-state model can only express as a melee immunity lifted by the gloves. Not modelled: the ashes that swallow any ammunition but ice arrows, which costs supplies rather than damage.

quotes: Kamil is weak to fire spells, but is immune to all other magic damage and effects
can only otherwise be damaged with Water spells or any kind of Ranged weapon
Fareed possesses the unique ability to disarm players who are not wearing ice gloves when they are attacking him close up
this is not possible for melee users as players who use melee will have their weapon unequipped since they are in close distance

description: Holy water damages demons and nothing else. The restriction outlives the damage formula this engine dropped, so a loadout holding holy water scores zero against a non-demon rather than being priced as an ordinary thrown weapon.

quotes: it will only deal damage against demons

description: The Warriors' Guild animated armours are immune to Ranged and Magic, leaving melee as the only style that scores against them. Keyed by monster id to the seven guild variants: the Tarn's Lair animated armour shares the name but is a separate monster carrying heavy magic and ranged defence and no immunity.

quotes: Like all other animated armour variants, it is immune to Ranged and Magic attacks.
Animated armour can be created and fought in the Warriors' Guild by using a full helm, platebody, and platelegs of the same type of metal on one of the magical animators.

description: Cyclopes inside the Warriors' Guild are immune to Ranged and Magic and must be fought with melee. Keyed by monster id because the Cyclops name is shared with level-81 monsters outside the guild that carry no immunity, so a name match would misdirect.

quotes: cyclopes found in these areas are immune to Ranged and Magic attacks and must be fought with melee combat.

description: Mother, the Weiss troll boss, is immune to Magic, so every magic loadout scores zero against her. Keyed by her monster id.

quotes: Mother is immune to magic

description: The Chambers of Xeric tightrope room's deathly rangers and mages stand on a platform across the rope, where no melee weapon can be brought to bear, so every melee loadout scores zero against them. This is a blanket melee immunity rather than a reach row because halberd reach does not close the gap either. The wiki describes the platform and counts the tightrope among the raid's Ranged rooms rather than its melee ones, but nowhere states the unreachability itself, so that half rests on in-game behaviour and stands unsourced. Not modelled: the room's tolerance and stalled-damage timing, and the keystone killing any survivors outright, neither of which steady-state DPS can express.

quotes: stand on a platform with a tightrope running in between
Ranged is used throughout the raid at Olm's final phase, Vespula, Vasa, the magic Vanguard, Shamans, Mystics, Muttadiles, and Tightrope.

description: The Fire Warrior of Lesarkus takes damage only from a ranged attack made with ice arrows equipped: the arrows themselves, and also darts or throwing knives thrown while the ice arrows sit in the ammo slot, which is why the escape reads the ammo slot rather than the weapon. Not modelled: the ring of recoil the article names as the one other source of damage, which is not an attack this model prices.

quotes: He is intended to only be damageable by firing the ice arrows that are collected in the icy caverns within the temple.
However, he can also be damaged by darts and throwing knives, provided that the ice arrows are equipped at the time.
He can also be damaged with rings of recoil.

description: TzKal-Zuk stands off the player's platform, so melee never reaches him and only Ranged and Magic score. Keyed by id, which covers the Normal and Enraged bestiary rows alike since both carry 7706. Not modelled: the shield the fight supplies, the Jal healers, or any part of the wave.

quotes: As TzKal-Zuk is isolated from the platform the player is on, it cannot be attacked with melee. Only ranged or magic attacks will be able to reach Zuk.
